source_state: Uncommitted driving-course diagnostic pass. Reports were built before the final header-only render text edit; simulation and diagnostics sources are unchanged. The manifest includes the final header text.
notes: Five isolated courses plus the ordinary seeded duel. Each case clones one native world and controller state into unchanged CPU, neutral axis and held-axis continuations.
A blocked duel is captured after 60 consecutive blocked-ground ticks, without resetting either controller or changing combat policy.

Each continuation runs 720 ticks. Reports measure signed net horizontal progress, pitch, actual wheel motion/spring lengths, support and route refusal. Native support, motor limits, collisions and terrain lifecycle remain active.
All 32 cases repeat the full initialization/capture prefix and all three continuations, including native snapshot identity and full report equality.
The slope is nominally 20 degrees sampled on the existing 0.5-unit interpolated terrain grid; it contains local 45-degree faces. This is not a smooth-ramp climbing limit.

The rubble starts as released grains, all of which redeposit during the 120-tick settling prefix in these runs. It tests the resulting uneven footing, not sustained loose-pile traction. Weak/Strong are retained controls and do not activate meaningful bank/impact failure in this fixture.
Held drive retains the stored CPU mode/history; those mode counts do not describe newly evaluated decisions in an overridden trial.
Held input can change later combat outcomes. The ordinary-duel neutral control is retained to expose uncommanded motion. Failing a held-input trial does not prove all driving maneuvers would fail.

No driving policy or suspension tuning in this pass. All 14 existing duel, hillside, roof and barrage benchmark hashes match the preceding build; their incidental timing values are not used for performance claims.
